title: RAI Policy Guardrails
summary: Define autonomy levels by risk, implement human-in-the-loop workflows, enforce least-privilege access, block policy violations, and design complete accountability systems.

blocks.text: **RAI guardrails operate at the OUTPUT layer and override user authorization.** Even a fully authorized user cannot cause the agent to produce policy-violating output.

items: Blocks: harmful content, content propagating bias, privacy-violating outputs, ethical AI violations
Security policies: same principle — override user requests, not the other way around
Compliance policies: GDPR, SOX, PCI constraints enforced even against legitimate-seeming requests
Correct behavior: block → explain policy violation → escalate if needed

blocks.text: **Critical:** User authorization ≠ policy override. Authorization lets a user make a request; RAI/security policies can still block the output.
